body_markdown:
A custom 1979 Chevrolet El Camino, known as the SS Monte Mino, will soon be recreated in 1:64 scale by Mattel after being crowned the winner of the 2026 Hot Wheels Legends Tour.


Owner Matt McEntegart not only widened the El Camino body modeled on the Monte Carlo, but he also mounted it to a 2008 Corvette chassis. After prototyping the body using foam and creating molds, he produced the bodywork in red-tinted forged carbon fiber, painting much of it deep maroon while leaving the bed and other elements exposed. With the El Camino and ‘Vette’s dimensions being rather different, McEntegart had to devise a 12-inch stretch to the chassis.


The Corvette V-8 makes its presence known with exposed velocity stacks; there’s air suspension and monster 22-inch, deep-dished rims. The interior is a stunning mix of red leather and tartan cloth. McEntegart did almost all the work himself, putting “thousands of hours” into the build.

Hot Wheels


His reward is that the SS Monte Mino will now become part of the Hot Wheels Garage of Legends and be produced as a limited-edition collectible model. It’s the first time since 2022 that a car from the U.S. has won the coveted title; the 2026 Tour traveled to 19 countries, including 12 stops in America.


“What makes Hot Wheels Legends Tour so special is its ability to bring automotive communities together and celebrate the incredible talent of builders around the world,” says Ted Wu, General Manager and Global Head of Vehicles and Building Sets at Mattel. “Matt’s El Camino stood out for its bold design and craftsmanship, and we’re honored to turn his passion project into an official Hot Wheels die-cast car for fans to play and collect around the world.”


The runners-up include Sandranto Hertanu of Indonesia, with a 1961 Mini pickup, and Andrea Cionco of Italy, with a wide-bodied 1995 Mazda MX-5.
